segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics news digest from October 29th, 2026.
Today we cover the physical intelligence valuation, new AI models, and funding for physical AI training.
Tune in for the latest!
From Humanoids Daily, Physical Intelligence Reportedly Seeks $1B at a $20B Valuation.
This report details the recent funding pursuit and valuation discussions involving the company Physical Intelligence.
The organization is reportedly seeking at least one billion dollars in funding based on a valuation of approximately twenty billion dollars.
The company has made its models available to external developers through an API beta for training and inference purposes.
This access facilitates the development of applications utilizing Physical Intelligence's models and infrastructure, emphasizing a shared intelligence layer across various robot bodies.
The company's objective is to establish a foundation model by aggregating learning from diverse robot experiences.
Existing investors Avenir and Lux Capital are reportedly engaged in discussions regarding leading the forthcoming financing round.
This development signals an increasing focus on unifying physical intelligence into a generalized, foundational model for robotics applications.
From Humanoids Daily, "AGIBOT Introduces Worken, New AI Models and G2 Max at Innovation Day 2026".
This report details the unveiling of new AI models, hardware, and productivity frameworks at the Innovation Day 2026 event.
The company introduced Worken, a metric for robot productivity calculated by the formula Worken equals Active Robots times Autonomous Working Hours times the Output Efficiency Ratio.

Demonstrations included new hardware such as the AHA3, which incorporates locomotion, interaction, and task execution functions, alongside new AI models including GO-3 Preview for reasoning and prediction and WITA-Omni 1.0 for human-robot interaction.
The G2 Max robot was presented, designed for industrial handling with a forty kilogram capacity and an adjustable working height.
Additionally, the Link-U OS 1.0 is under development with an open-source roadmap intended for full open-sourcing by the close of 2026.
This development signals advancements in measurable robotics and human-robot collaboration technologies.
From Robotics & Automation News, Maxinsights raises thirty million dollars to build a training data platform for physical artificial intelligence.

The company has expanded its physical AI data platform, which generates training data by compensating contractors to record real-world activities, achieving a total collection of over two million hours of human activity, with one and a half million hours being made ready for AI applications.

The process involves utilizing systems such as MaxLoop for quality control and MaxGlove for capturing tactile information, including grip force, to ensure the real-world data exposed AI models to variations found in actual homes and workplaces.
Maxinsights currently serves more than thirty customers, including various AI labs and foundation model developers.
This methodology provides a method for acquiring diverse, realistic training data essential for robust physical AI development.
The industry should monitor developments in real-world data acquisition for training advanced models.
From The Robot Report, "What Symbotic’s Walmart growth teaches robotics startups about anchor customers"
highlights the necessity for robotics startups to scrutinize anchor customer relationships.

The report examines how Symbotic's reliance on Walmart as a major customer underscores the importance of understanding contract terms such as continuity rights and sales limitations when assessing the true cost of servicing large accounts.
Growth strategy is advised to focus on understanding the field-load logic where pilot programs can reveal hidden field work costs and support needs.
Startups are encouraged to build repeatable processes that minimize dependency on single anchor customers for future demand.
Founders should model scenarios to determine growth potential while prioritizing contractual control and financial resilience over sheer customer volume.
This signals a shift for the AI and tech industry toward valuing contractual understanding and diversified revenue streams over singular large-scale customer acquisition.
From Humanoids Daily, Unitree’s Quarterly Revenue Surges 70% as R&D Spending Weighs on Profit.
This report details Unitree's third-quarter financial performance, noting a substantial increase in revenue alongside significant investment in research and development.
Unitree recorded third-quarter revenue of six hundred sixty-five million yuan, representing a seventy percent year-on-year increase.

Concurrently, research and development spending rose by two hundred forty-nine point six percent to twelve hundred seventy million yuan, with the focus of this expenditure being embodied-intelligence models and computing capacity.
Net profit attributable to shareholders declined by seventeen point four percent to one hundred twelve point seven million yuan.
This data indicates that sales expansion occurred alongside heavy investment in future technological development.
The figures suggest ongoing high investment rates within the robotics and artificial intelligence sector.
From The Robot Report, "WorldOracle Tests Whether World Models Can Reliably Predict Real-World Executions".
This report evaluates action-conditioned world models by comparing their predictions against real-world executions under identical starting conditions and action sequences.
The evaluation assessed the models' accuracy in predicting object positions, movements, and the consequences of actions, including instances of failure.
The benchmark utilized multiple scoring metrics, including Physical State Correctness and Interaction Spatial Alignment, to detail prediction errors.

Results indicated that while predictions regarding robot arm motion were often reasonable, object positions frequently differed from actual reality, and performance diminished across extended operational sequences.
Developers can contribute by submitting predictions from various model types to receive specific feedback for model refinement.
This research highlights ongoing challenges in achieving precise, long-term prediction in dynamic physical environments for artificial intelligence systems.
From Humanoids Daily, Audi tests Agile Robots mobile humanoids for automotive parts sequencing.
This report details an initiative to employ mobile humanoid robots for sorting and arranging automotive components within a production setting.
Agile Robots provided the mobile humanoids, while virtual testing utilized a virtual twin supported by Dassault Systèmes and NVIDIA.
The system integrates dual-arm manipulation and a mobile base designed to manage varied and unsorted components in logistics environments.
The process involves the robots picking components from containers and arranging them for subsequent automotive assembly.
Future viability of the system will be determined by the consistent demonstration of physical performance and operational costs.
This development indicates progress in applying mobile manipulation systems to complex industrial logistics.
Further assessment of performance benchmarks is anticipated in the near future.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Neura Robotics and TUM open €17 million RoboGym and unveil new humanoid".
This report details the opening of a robotics center and the introduction of a new humanoid robot.
The center, known as the TUM RoboGym, combines research, training, and industrial applications across various sectors.
The facility facilitates robot training in tasks such as handling boxes and loading components by utilizing real-world data, human demonstrations, and simulation methodologies.
Furthermore, the newly unveiled 4NE1 Gen 4 humanoid robot features lighter construction and incorporates advanced Smart Limbs powered by Neuron AI.
This initiative seeks to advance physical artificial intelligence capabilities and establish an international network of such training facilities.
The development signals a progression in embodied AI and the expansion of practical robotics training.
From Humanoid.guide, "Xpeng Iron batteries enter small batch output ahead of robot".
This report concerns the production status of batteries intended for the Xpeng Iron humanoid robot, detailing the commencement of small batch manufacturing.
Xpeng's vice president announced this battery update at the SAE conference, describing a solid-state battery developed specifically for the robot's confined space.
This battery is claimed to offer protection against thermal runaway spread and has successfully withstood impact testing procedures.
Although the precise battery chemistry remains unconfirmed, some reports indicate the utilization of a solid-liquid hybrid technology owing to commercialization delays.
Xpeng maintains a target for mass production of the Iron robot by the close of 2026.
This development signals progress in energy solutions for advanced robotics.
Further developments regarding the robot's production timeline should be monitored.
From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control".
This story details how living digital twins, enhanced by artificial intelligence, achieve synchronization between dynamic representations of industrial operations and real-time control.
Agentic AI facilitates systems moving toward industrial homeostasis through autonomous adjustments while maintaining human oversight for goal definition and alignment monitoring.
This synchronization is established by linking real-time sensor data via a digital thread, integrating predictive models and artificial intelligence insights.
Real-world implementations demonstrate AI optimizing energy consumption, improving quality, and ensuring asset health across diverse sectors.
Future integration focuses on pairing physical AI with robotics to create interconnected industrial networks that improve resilience.
This development signals a shift toward deeply integrated, self-regulating industrial systems.
From The Robot Report, North American robot orders climb 24.8% in Q3 of 2026, says A3.
This report details the growth observed in the North American robotics market during the third quarter of 2026.
Orders increased by twenty-four point eight percent in units and twenty-six point one percent in value for the quarter.
The total number of robot orders for the first nine months of 2026 reached twenty-eight thousand nine hundred eighty-four units valued at approximately one point eight nine billion dollars.
This expansion was fueled by demand across the automotive, semiconductor, life sciences, and plastics/rubber sectors, indicating a diversified market expansion.
Collaborative robots specifically experienced a significant rise of fifty-six percent in the third quarter, representing sixteen point seven percent of all units ordered.
This positive trend aligns with expanding manufacturing activity.
Continued market growth is anticipated as manufacturing activity remains strong.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Faraday Future chairman: Moving from Chinese robot sourcing to US manufacturing"
reports on Faraday Future's strategic shift toward establishing domestic manufacturing capabilities within the United States.
The company plans to bring a US robot factory online by the end of 2026 and launch its first US-assembled robot in February 2027.
This localization strategy is designed to improve supply-chain resilience, regulatory compliance, and quality control for the robotics products.
Faraday Future views vehicles and robotics as complementary components of a larger physical AI ecosystem, emphasizing the shared use of technologies such as artificial intelligence and perception.
Success for the organization is projected to be measured by establishing a sustainable US-based physical AI and robotics ecosystem rather than focusing solely on revenue metrics.
This move signals a growing focus on integrating physical manufacturing with advanced artificial intelligence development in the technology sector.
From Humanoids Daily, Robbyant’s Embodied AI Challenge Will Send 15 Teams to a Real-Robot Final in Shanghai.
This report details an upcoming hackathon competition focused on adapting vision-language-action models to physical robotic tasks.

The competition will feature fifteen teams participating in a forty-eight hour event in Shanghai where competitors will utilize AgileX Robotics’ Cobot Magic platform to adapt models based on the open-source LingBot-VLA 2.0 model.
Over one thousand eight hundred teams have registered for the event.
The competition seeks to measure the effectiveness of vision-language-action models when applied to real-world robotic execution.
Final task design and scoring criteria for the challenge are currently being finalized by Robbyant.
This event provides a benchmark for real-world application of embodied artificial intelligence in robotics.
From MIT News - Robotics, "A soft robot could help doctors diagnose and treat disorders of the small intestine".
This story details the development of a robotic enteroscope designed to navigate the narrow small intestine for improved diagnosis and treatment.
MIT engineers developed a soft robot inspired by snake locomotion, utilizing flexible actuators and specially coated surfaces to gain traction on the intestinal lining.
The device is equipped with instruments for imaging, drug delivery, biopsies, and polyp removal.
Research endeavors to surpass the limitations of existing procedures such as double balloon enteroscopy when evaluating the long intestinal segment.
Animal studies have successfully verified the robot's movement and the operational functionality of its integrated tools.
This advancement suggests potential for minimally invasive surgical techniques in gastrointestinal diagnostics.
The ongoing research indicates future developments in endoscopic robotics are anticipated.
From The Robot Report, "Warp Sciences emerges from stealth, to apply robotics to drug research".
This segment details the recent funding and operational focus of Warp Sciences in the field of pharmaceutical research.
Warp Sciences successfully raised two hundred fifteen million dollars to establish chemistry infrastructure for sovereign biotechnology with the objective of accelerating drug discovery.
The company is developing a United States-based contract research organization that integrates chemists, robotics, and artificial intelligence to perform the synthesis and testing of molecules.
The methodology involves generating real-world data to train artificial intelligence, which is intended to create more capable laboratories and expedite the transition from hypothesis to experiment.
Warp concentrates on lead optimization analog synthesis, allowing clients to maintain control over sensitive research within the United States through automation.
This advancement signifies a push toward integrating advanced robotics and AI into the core processes of pharmaceutical development.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, W-Bot!".
This segment reports on the introduction of a wheeled humanoid robot designed for tight space manipulation.
The robot measures one hundred seventy-eight centimeters in height and weighs sixty kilograms.
Yue Quan Bionics developed this robot utilizing a compact base and an articulated upper body incorporating folding joints to achieve a working reach from floor level up to two point two meters.
The system is equipped with multiple arms capable of lifting ten kilograms and sensory systems including depth cameras and LiDAR for environmental awareness.
Primary functions of the robot involve obstacle avoidance, sorting goods, and product assembly within confined environments.
This development indicates a focus on dexterity and reach in constrained settings for robotic applications.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, CYBORG H02!".
This segment reports on the specifications and production status of the CYBORG H02 robotic hand.
The device is a robotic hand manufactured by Cyborg Robotics in Guangdong, China, which features a design based on five fingers and a tendon mechanism driven by six electric motors.
The hand has a mass of 750 grams and dimensions measuring 248 by 114 by 52 millimeters.
Evaluation scores place the hand with a Humanoid.Guide Hand Score of seven out of ten, a Degrees of Freedom rating of three out of five, and a Strength rating of four out of five.
The product is currently in production with an advertised price of four thousand US dollars.
This development indicates ongoing advancements in the integration of complex electromechanical systems into robotic manipulation hardware.
Future developments in dexterity and cost-effective robotics are expected in this sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Mornine!".
This segment details the introduction of Mornine, a newly developed bipedal humanoid robot for commercial applications, which exhibits specific physical capabilities and manufacturing details.

Mornine is a 167 centimeter tall, 70 kilogram bipedal humanoid constructed with an aluminum alloy structure and electric joint actuators, featuring five fingers on each hand and forty degrees of freedom.

The robot is designed to perform tasks such as obstacle avoidance and sorting goods, operating at a maximum speed of three point six kilometers per hour and possessing a strength capacity of three kilograms.
Assessment indicates a low Humanoid Guide Skill Score of two out of ten, suggesting early-stage physical capabilities in navigation and manipulation.
Production of Mornine is currently underway in China with an approximate listed price of forty-one thousand four hundred US dollars.
This development signals ongoing progression in the creation of physically capable artificial entities within the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, TORCH HAND 2!".
This segment reports on the specifications and performance evaluation of the TORCH HAND 2 robotic hand.
The evaluation indicates that the device scores six out of ten in the Humanoid.Guide Hand Score, demonstrating a specific balance between dexterity and gripping power.
The TORCH HAND 2 measures two hundred millimeters by one hundred five millimeters by fifty millimeters and has a mass of zero point four eight kilograms.
The hand achieved a four out of five rating for degrees of freedom but received a two out of five rating for strength.
Advertised at six thousand five hundred US dollars, the design offers a commercially available option balancing these functional attributes for various tasks.
This progress suggests continued development in creating adaptable robotic manipulators for commercial application.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, NE01!".

This segment details the specifications and current capabilities of the NE01 humanoid robot developed by GENISOM AI, noting that it functions as a preliminary platform rather than a broadly capable worker.

The NE01 measures one hundred forty-five centimeters in height and weighs forty kilograms, constructed from an aluminum alloy structure incorporating integrated joint modules and equipped with a five hundred forty watt hour battery allowing for a two-hour operational runtime.
Testing demonstrated the robot's ability to perform obstacle avoidance and sort goods, although navigation and manipulation skills were assessed as very low.
The unit is currently cataloged as a prototype with an indicative price of twenty thousand United States dollars.
This development indicates ongoing research into the practical application and limitations of humanoid robotics in industrial settings.
And that’s all the circuits for today from the Robotics Digest.
Keep debugging your world, and we’ll see you tomorrow for more awesome tech updates.
Have a fantastic cycle!
